name: Moped
description: A two-wheeled motor vehicle, with or without pedals, whose electric motor produces less than 2,000 watts and can propel it past 20 mph on its own or keeps assisting a pedaling rider past 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Two tandem wheels, either of them at least 10 inches in diameter; pedals are optional (Delaware Code Title 21 §101(40))

Its electric motor produces less than 2,000 watts and can propel it faster than 20 mph by itself, or keeps assisting past 28 mph while the rider pedals; an electric bicycle is never a moped (Delaware Code Title 21 §101(40), as amended by House Substitute 1 for HB 439)
Since September 24, 2026 a moped is a motor vehicle rather than a bicycle, and an electric two-wheeler of 2,000 watts or more is a motorcycle (House Substitute 1 for HB 439)
Riders need a driver's license, carried while riding, but no motorcycle endorsement; a nonresident needs a valid license from their home state (Delaware Code Title 21 §4198M)
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a fastened helmet meeting the bicycle helmet standard (Delaware Code Title 21 §4198M)
Titled and registered with the DMV for $5 per three years, with a moped plate on the rear; registrations expire December 31 (Delaware Code Title 21 §4198M)
Exempt from safety inspection, but the DMV verifies the VIN of one first titled in another state (Delaware Code Title 21 §4198M)
No motor vehicle insurance required (Delaware Code Title 21 §4198M)
Barred from interstate and limited-access highways, even to cross them, and from railroad rights-of-way except to cross (Delaware Code Title 21 §4198M)
Barred from bike lanes, sidewalks and any pathway closed to motor vehicle traffic (Delaware Code Title 21 §4198M, as amended by House Substitute 1 for HB 439)
Bicycle traffic rules apply to it on public roads (Delaware Code Title 21 §4198M, as amended by House Substitute 1 for HB 439)

Sellers may not market or label it as an e-bike or claim it is legal on a public pathway or bike lane, and must disclose in writing its legal class, motor power in watts and brake horsepower, top speed, and that registration, license and insurance rules apply (House Substitute 1 for HB 439)
